title: Cold rebuild: umask
summary: Rebuild umask from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **umask** in *Owners, sudo and umask*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: `sudo echo "10.0.0.5 db" >> /etc/hosts` says *Permission denied*. Which fixes it?
steps.explain: `>>` is performed by your unprivileged shell before sudo runs. `tee` runs under sudo and opens the file itself. Option 2 has the same bug *and* would truncate the file.

steps.title: Rebuild umask cold
prompt: Write `string DefaultMode(string umask, bool isDirectory)` returning the 3-digit octal mode a new file or directory gets. `umask` is 3 or 4 octal digits (`"022"` or `"0027"`); only the last 3 matter.
Hint: parse octal with `Convert.ToInt32(s, 8)` and print with `Convert.ToString(n, 8)`, padded to 3 digits.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
